findings.title: Main receipt polling can associate a receipt with the wrong transaction

status.supplemental: Do not infer regression from sibling feature branches that have not integrated candidate receipt fix.

findings.scenario: The configured RPC returns an unrelated or misrouted successful receipt for a requested payment hash while the actual transaction is visible and still pending. Main only checks the optional destination and treats status 1 as success, so a receipt for another payment to the same router can be accepted.
findings.impact: The UI and local export may classify the requested payment as included without a receipt bound to that hash. This is an integrity/error-handling issue at the configured RPC boundary; it does not establish independent chain verification or an attacker-independent payment forgery.
findings.remediation: Retain the candidate's exact transactionHash validation and strict receipt status validation. Verify the ordinary payment and approval flows exercise those failures through submitTx.
findings.tests: wallet and payExec test sources remain unread in this lane; do not claim their coverage or execution.

findings.title: Main native sweep signs a freshly observed balance rather than the amount displayed for review
findings.scenario: A seller sees the current native balance and starts a direct sweep. The balance changes before the signing preflight finishes. Main uses the newly read balance to calculate value, without requiring it to equal the balance passed by the view.
findings.impact: The signed native transfer can move a different amount from the amount displayed when the action started. Existing destination checks and fee caps still apply; no theft or arbitrary destination bypass is claimed.
findings.remediation: Keep the candidate's equality check and explicit native fee preparation/confirmation. The single-use review should continue to bind destination, balance, nonce, fees, endpoint, manifest, replacement attempt and context until handoff.
findings.tests: Fully read sweep.reviewAuthority.test.ts:187–249, covering changed balances before signing, delayed reads, same-nonce replacement, and deposits after the checked snapshot. Native review and Sweep view tests remain unread. No execution.

findings.title: Main in-flight sweeps do not invalidate signing when the visible review changes
findings.scenario: During a slow vault or RPC step, the seller changes the destination or selected sweep context. The destination input remains editable. Main guards the seller session, but its captured action proceeds with the earlier review and the helper receives no live review callback.
findings.impact: Main can sign or hand off the earlier destination/context while the view displays a newer choice. This is a stale-action authorization mismatch; existing transaction validation still applies to the captured fields.
findings.remediation: Preserve the candidate's scope identity, cancellation signals and assertReviewCurrent checks through key derivation, preflight, signing and pre-handoff. Once handoff starts, retain any returned or uncertain result even if the view subsequently changes.
findings.tests: Fully read sweep.reviewAuthority.test.ts:96–185, including review revocation before derivation, during RPC/signing, and preservation of outcomes once handoff began. UI-level review-scope tests remain unread. No execution.

findings.title: Malformed ERC20 boolean simulation data is reported as a successful dry run
findings.scenario: A configured node returns nonempty hexadecimal data for a direct ERC20 transfer simulation that is not a canonical ABI boolean. Main and the combined candidate classify any such return other than an exact false word as successful.
findings.impact: The UI loses the unavailable-simulation warning and can misdescribe the preflight. The helper already permits unavailable simulation by policy, so this finding does not establish a new authorization bypass or fund-loss path.
findings.remediation: Include #305's canonical boolean classification: legacy empty return remains accepted; canonical true is accepted; canonical false is refused; other nonempty data is unavailable. Preserve the distinction between an unavailable simulation and a confirmed successful simulation.
findings.tests: txGuard.test.ts fully read in e22 (1–164) and #305 (1–183 via full base and complete diff). Added malformed-bool and generic-call cases reviewed. No execution.

findings.title: Receipt import description overstates recipient comparison for minimal receipts

status.main: not present under mandatory recipient format

findings.scenario: A payer has prepared a payment and imports a valid signed receipt that intentionally omits its one-time address. The view passes an expected address, but the shared binding function intentionally skips comparison when the receipt lacks that field.
findings.impact: The introduction says a prepared one-time address is checked, although no recipient comparison occurs for this permitted minimal receipt. Signature, invoice digest, chain, asset and amount checks still occur; the success message and export correctly describe a seller attestation rather than independent payment proof.
findings.remediation: Make the introductory claim conditional on the receipt carrying an address, or display which optional fields were actually compared. Keep the intentional privacy-preserving omission.
findings.tests: Package worker read the intended minimal-receipt acceptance tests. This lane independently inspected package binding lines139–163, full Pay and full ReceiptPanel; relevant web receipt tests remain unread. No execution.

known_hardening.title: parseUnits runtime type and precision validation
known_hardening.scenario: A caller violates the TypeScript contract by supplying a non-string amount or invalid precision. The helper can throw instead of returning undefined. Reviewed production callers supply strings and compiled or fixed valid precisions; an externally reachable misuse was not established.
known_hardening.impact: Helper API robustness and error predictability; not a confirmed production security exploit.
known_hardening.tests: Full e22 format.test.ts1–78 and #3031–92 read; added invalid-type/precision tests cover the helper contract. No execution.

cross_lane_confirmations.title: #300 omits wallet prop at real Pay callers, hiding all attempt recovery controls
cross_lane_confirmations.novelty: new #300 integration regression; custody lane owns canonical finding
cross_lane_confirmations.scenario: After a wallet attempt, the journal retains the action until an explicit review/clear. In #300 WalletAttempts hides records and clear controls unless wallet is supplied, but both Pay call sites still omit it, including after connection.
cross_lane_confirmations.impact: The intended in-app recovery is unreachable and repeat requests for the same invoice remain blocked in the tab. Payment keys are scoped to invoice and chain rather than account, so merely reconnecting does not clear that block. No funds-loss claim.
cross_lane_confirmations.remediation: Pass the current wallet into real core Pay call sites and exercise the actual view with a retained attempt. Custody owns the detailed test follow-up.
